newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil products outlook - exports prop heating o.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil products outlook - exports prop heating o.

text.p: European oil products look well supported over the next week or so as arbitrage outlets cream off more European gasoline, naphtha and possibly gas oil, traders said.
The key middle distillates market, which includes winter heating oil, is underpinned not only by a potential arbitrage window to the U.S., but also to Asia.

Shipping brokers said on Friday that Cargill, the dominant long in the recent IPE gas oil duel, fixed a 49,000 tonne cargo from northwest Europe to India, and another trader was heard on Thursday having sold another European cargo to Singapore.
While gas oil arbitrage numbers were theoretically workable, it was hard to predict where U.S. markets would open on Monday after last week's extended closure for the Thanksgiving holiday.
Adding to the short term uncertainty is the outcome of the duel on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) between two traders, Cargill and AIC.
"It could be a very volatile week," one London-based trader said. "There is a lot of uncertainty in the market -- uncertainty about the IPE delivery, uncertainty about the weather in the States."
Strikes at Elf's three French refineries are expected to continue to exert a bearish pressure on prices, as French domestic consumption of diesel and gasoline dwindles.
But cold weather may strengthen the backbone of this month's small gas oil price rally.
Private forecaster Weather Services Corp saw temperatures in the next five days near to or below normal for most of Europe.
Even gasoline may firm this week after recent exports to the U.S. helped mop up excess supply.
Rotterdam barges could move back towards $220 a tonne after hovering mostly below $215 last week, dealers said. "At these levels the market will be supported by crude," a broker said.
He said premiums for gasoline above crude were currently low and any gains on Brent would be reflected in gasoline markets.
Naphtha is also well supported. Bad weather at the Algerian port of Skikda has delayed liftings of at least three 60,000-tonne cargoes.

Asian prices are likely to stay strong too, mopping up marginal barrels from the east, and arbitrage demand from the U.S. continues to draw off European cargoes. Traders see U.S. interest stretching into January.
High sulphur cracked fuel is likely to stay firm this week with slow interest balanced by lack of supplies. But much will depend upon Russian supplies, which still cap the market.
Prices were likely to stay close to the $120 cif NWE.
Turkey and Portugal tendered to buy up to 125,000 tonnes in December and January, lower than in previous tenders.
Low sulphur fuel is tight in early December.
